This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 and 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.

2. The brief facts of the case is as under;
SCCH-5 That on 09.06.2023 at about 6.45 a.m. while travelling in a KIA Sonata Car bearing Reg.No.KA-52-N- 7863 at underpass, near Byrapura Village, NH-75 Road, Alur Tqluk, Hassan District, the driver of the said car driving the car at high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed against opposite Container Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AN-1598, due to the said impact, he has sustained injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Janapriya Hospital, wherein he took treatment as inpatient since 09.06.2023 to 27.06.2023, for which he has spent an amount of Rs.5,50,000/- for medical expenses, Rs.40,000/- towards food and nourishment and Rs.40,000/-
towards conveyance.
3. At the time of the accident, he was aged about 32 years, hale and healthy, working as a private employee, thereby earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.,

due to the SCCH-5 accidental injuries sustained by him, he is unable to work, thereby sustained loss of income and also he is not able to walk, run,
stand, sit and he is getting pain at injuries spot.
Out of this accident crime No.120/2023 is registered against the car driver by the Alur Police, Sakaleshpura, Hassan District for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 and 338 of IPC.
R1 is the insurer, R2 is owner of the said car, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% p.a.
4.
On service of notice, Respondent No.1/insurer has appeared and filed written statement and denied the averments of the petition.

He has stated that, petition is liable to be dismissed for non-joinder of necessary parties as the owner and insurer of the lorry bearing Reg.No.KA- SCCH-5 01-AN-1598 have not been made as parties to the said proceedings.
He has admitted issuance of insurance policy bearing No.OG-23-1021-1825-00068569 i.e., Private Car Policy - Bundled in favour of respondent No.2 for the period from 31.03.2023 to 30.03.2026.
Further he is entitled to take shelter under Sec.170 of M.V.Act.

Further the driver of the insured vehicle was not Sunil Kumar.R vs Bajaj All Gen Ins Co Ltd on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64344664/
2 having valid driving license to drive the same as on the date of accident.

SCCH-5 ::ISSUES::
1.

Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 09.06.2023 at about 6.45 a.m. near Byrapura Village, NH-5 Road, Alur Taluk, Hassan District, due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-52-N-7863 by driver, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?

6. In order to prove his case, petitioner himself deposed his evidence as PW-1, examined Medical Record Officer of Janapriya Hospital as PW-2, Dr.Chidanand K.J.C. Orthopaedic Surgeon at Sanjay Gandhi Hospital as PW-3 and marked 18 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.18 and closed his evidence.
On the other hand, respondent No.1 has not adduced any evidence.

 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 ::REASONS::

Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated here.

In support of his case, he exhibited copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of crime details form, spot mahazar with sketch is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of reply is marked as SCCH-5 Ex.P.4, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.6.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1 to PW-3 and records those have marked i.e., FIR, complaint,
crime details form, spot mahazar with sketch, reply, IMV Report and charge sheet corroborates the case of the petitioner about causing of the accident dated 09.06.2023 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
10.

Per contra, except filing of written statement, respondent No.1 has not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Since in the SCCH-5 absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioner about causing of the injuries to the petitioner out of the accident held on 09.06.2023 at about 6.45 a.m. at underpass, near Byrapura village, NH-75 Road, Alur Taluk,
Hassan District while travelling in a KIA Sonata car bearing Reg.No.KA-52-N-7863 due to rash and negligent driving of driver of the said car.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioner.
11. The police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the car driver.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioner, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the SCCH-5 above issue No.1 in his favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:-

As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained open type frcture of right leg bones, frcture of multiple ribs, fracture of nasal bones, severe head injury, chest injury,
pneumomediastinum with facial injury, for which he underwent treatment in the form of ORIF with plate and screws.

In this regard he has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.7,
discharge summary marked as Ex.P.8 issued by Janapriya Hospital, wherein he took treatment as inpatient since 09.06.2023 to 27.06.2023.

He also furnished medical prescriptions marked as Ex.P.10, 3 photographs with 1 CD marked as Ex.P.11, X-ray Films marked as Ex.P.12 and CT-Scan films marked as Ex.P.13.
SCCH-5 13.

The Medical Record Officer at Janapriya Hospital is examined as PW-2, who has exhibited authorization letter marked as Ex.P.14, copy of MLC Extract with Police Intimation marked as Ex.P.15 and case sheet marked as Ex.P.16.
Further Dr.Chidanand K.J.C. Orthopaedic Surgeon at Sanjay Gandhi Hospital is examined as PW-3 and got exhibited clinical notes marked as Ex.P.17 and X-ray Films marked as Ex.P.18.
He has assessed whole body disability from lower limb at the rate of 15%.
In cross-examination he has categorically admitted that, he has not treated the petitioner.
PW-3 further deposed that, now fractures is united with implant and in younger age healing process will be faster.

Further deposed that, as per the discharge summary there is no ankle joint injury,
ankle and knee joint will play a vital role in movements of a person.
He SCCH-5 has also made clinical examination.
Under such circumstances, considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and also by relying on citation reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343 between Rajkumar V/s.

Ajay Kumar, the functional disability of the petitioner is considered at the rate of 12% for the Sunil Kumar.R vs Bajaj All Gen Ins Co Ltd on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64344664/

Accordingly they are not applicable to the present case on hand.
19. Further admittedly for incurring the expenses towards medical treatment, petitioner has marked Ex.P.9 medial bills.
As per the said documents, he has spent Rs.2,20,660/- for grievous injuries sustained by him in Janapriya Hospital.

Contrary to the said fact, there is no rebuttal evidence by the respondent No.1, in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to accept the case of the petitioner with regard to entitlement of medical expenses, as he has spent an amount of Rs.2,20,660/- as per Ex.P.9 medical bills.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for compensation for the said bills.

22. In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.OG-23- 1021-1825-00068569 which is valid for the period from 31.03.2033 to 30.03.2026 in respect of KIA Sonata Car bearing Reg.No.KA-52-N-7863, the alleged accident was SCCH-5 occurred on 09.06.2023 it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force, so that, R1/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
23. Issue No.3:
For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:

::ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.6,26,170/- (Rupees Six Lakhs Twenty Six Thousand One Hundred Seventy only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.1 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
SCCH-5

The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
